_what: Notes on how the certified engine builds the PolicyEngine counterpart in lane uk-childcare-100k (CenTax and CBP claims alike), and what was verified about each certified pair the lane has run. Each note cites the engine file it was read from and names, in variants, the pairs it was checked on; it attaches only to those pairs' results. verified_pairs holds each pair's own statements; ingest refuses an artifact whose pair is not listed, so no note written for one pair attaches to another. The measured numbers that go with them are written onto each result by scorecard_db/ingest_uk_childcare_100k.py from the artifact beside this file, not copied here.

annotations.text: Both offers are England's. policyengine-uk tests country == ENGLAND for the extended, universal and targeted hours but not for Tax-Free Childcare, which it applies across the UK. The counterpart sums each head for people in English households (the household's country projected onto its members); ingest checks that no free-hours head moves outside England, and states the Tax-Free Childcare change outside England.
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.89.2 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py, universal_childcare_entitlement/universal_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py and targeted_childcare_entitlement/targeted_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py (in_england); variables/gov/hmrc/tax_free_childcare/ (no country test); policyengine_uk 2.132.6 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement_qualifying_child.py, universal_childcare_entitlement/universal_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py and targeted_childcare_entitlement/targeted_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py (in_england); variables/gov/hmrc/tax_free_childcare/ (no country test); pipeline/compute_uk_childcare_100k.py england_masks; results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json sums_gbp_england

annotations.text: policyengine-uk 2.89.2 switches a child's universal and targeted hours off once the family is eligible for the extended hours, and values the extended hours at the family's drawn weekly usage (maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage). The counterpart sums all three entitlements, so the universal hours a newly eligible family loses are netted out rather than double-counted. policyengine-uk#2177 (merged 12 October 2026, after the pin) changed this, closing policyengine-uk#1930.

policyengine-uk 2.132.6 keeps a child's universal and targeted hours once the family is eligible for the extended hours (policyengine-uk#2177). The extended hours pay only the part of the child's working-parent total above them, so the child's funded hours are the larger of the two. Where the family's standalone take-up of the universal or targeted offer is false, the engine pays that offer out of the working-parent total, so only once the family takes up the extended hours. Removing the limit therefore never lowers a child's universal or targeted hours: on this pair it raises universal spending and leaves targeted spending unchanged in every year (both measured).
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.132.6 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement_per_child.py (max_ of the rounded total less universal and targeted, and 0), universal_childcare_entitlement/universal_childcare_entitlement.py and targeted_childcare_entitlement/targeted_childcare_entitlement.py (min_(base_value, where(standalone_claim, base_value, working_parent_total))), the two eligibility files (no ~has_extended_childcare); https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk/pull/2177; results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json sums_gbp_england, worlds.free_hours minus worlds.baseline

annotations.text: The offer starts at 9 months. The engine's extended-hours scale starts at age 0.75, but every age on this pair is a whole number of years, so a child under 1 has age 0 and no child under 1 receives extended hours in any world or year (both measured). microcosm#1126 records the same for the Microcosm release.
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.89.2 parameters/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/hours.yaml (threshold 0.75 from 2025); policyengine_uk 2.132.6 the same file and parameters/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/young_child_minimum_age.yaml (0.75 from 2024-09-01); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json counts.people_with_fractional_age and counts.children_under_one_receiving_extended (0 in every world and year); https://github.com/PolicyEngine/microcosm/issues/1126

pair-pe6.11.0_uk2.132.6_microcosm-uk-202.diagnosis: About two-thirds of the excess over CenTax comes from this cut's take-up draws. A family above £100,000 can hold extended take-up true and universal take-up false. It receives no universal hours under current law, though those hours have no income limit, and receives them only once the reform makes it eligible for the extended hours. Every pound of the universal change falls on such children: £0.143bn in 2027-28 and £0.159bn in 2029-30. microcosm#1338 (merged 23 October 2026, after this cut) nests the universal draw under the extended one, so a family that claims the extended hours also claims the universal hours. The extended hours alone move £0.864bn and £1.065bn on this pair, 8% and 9% above CenTax, and this run does not explain that remainder.
